metadata.title: Partial Trace — Side-by-Side True, Purity Bar Misleads

beats.narration_text: Bonjour. Liam here, in for Bear. Claude wrote this visualization of the partial trace — two density matrix heatmaps side by side, one slider, the arithmetic of tracing away a qubit playing out live. Today we judge the viz, not the physics.

props.segment: Partial Trace — Tracing Away One Qubit
props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for the partial trace of an entangled two-qubit system.
output: ✓ Partial Trace — Tracing Away One Qubit Kills All Coherence
✓ D3 heatmaps: 4×4 joint ρ_AB, 2×2 reduced ρ_A
✓ θ slider 0°→45°, purity and entropy bars

beats.narration_text: Three panels. Left: a four-by-four density matrix ρ_AB — sixteen cells, basis labels |00⟩ through |11⟩ on both axes, each cell shaded proportionally with its numerical value printed inside. Center: the two-by-two reduced matrix ρ_A after tracing out qubit B, same encoding. Right: two horizontal bars for purity and entropy, and a static text box. One θ slider at the bottom. A readout strip reads the current numbers.

The θ slider drives the state — cosine θ times |00⟩ plus sine θ times |11⟩ — sweeping from the Bell state at 45° toward the product state at 0°. At the Bell state, four cells in ρ_AB light up at 0.500: the two diagonal corners and the two off-diagonal corners at row zero column three and row three column zero. Those are the coherences. Watch the sweep: the coherences in ρ_AB shrink. The off-diagonal cells in ρ_A stay beige — exactly zero — the whole way across. The partial trace sums those coherences away.

Two things earn their keep. First: the side-by-side layout. At the Bell state, ρ_AB lights up those off-diagonal coherence cells at 0.500. Scan right to ρ_A: those same positions show exactly zero on beige. Drag the slider anywhere and they stay there. No equation needed — the vanishing is visible, persistent, and unambiguous. Second: the double encoding. Every nonzero cell gets both a shade of ink proportional to its value and the printed number inside. You never guess whether a dark cell is 0.3 or 0.7 — the digit is right there, usable as a fact-check against your own calculation.

Three real problems. First: the purity bar maps purity from 0.5 to 1.0, not from 0 to 1 — but those limits are invisible. At the Bell state the bar looks nearly empty. A viewer reads near-zero purity. In reality, 0.5 is the minimum possible purity for any qubit — the bar's left edge is not near-zero, it is maximally mixed. The hidden domain creates a reliable misconception. Second: the state label reads 'partially entangled' for 43 of 45 degrees. From 1° to 44°, the same string — no information across most of the slider range. Third: θ is never defined. The label shows '0° = product state, 45° = Bell state' without the state formula. The parameter is a black box to anyone who doesn't already know it.

Let's recap with Claude. The side-by-side panels make the partial trace visible without an equation — ρ_AB's off-diagonals trace away and ρ_A stays diagonal throughout. Worth using. But the purity bar hides its own domain: its left edge is 0.5, not 0, and nowhere is that labeled. Students read maximum entanglement as near-zero purity. Fix the axis first. Best use: right after the trace formula, as a confirmation tool for students who can already read a density matrix.

beats.narration_text: I have a partial trace visualization showing ρ_AB and ρ_A side by side with a θ slider. Two fixes. First: the purity bar maps purity from 0.5 to 1.0 but carries no axis labels — a viewer reads the Bell state as near-zero purity when 0.5 is the minimum possible for a qubit. Add endpoint labels showing 0.5 on the left edge and 1.0 on the right edge of the bar. Second: add a live state formula display below the slider showing psi equals cosine theta times ket 00 plus sine theta times ket 11, with the actual numerical coefficients cos θ and sin θ updated as you drag. Keep the single-file HTML format.
